chunks: Those who were left behind rejoiced at their places of sitting, contrary to the Messenger of Allah, and disliked that they should strive with their wealth and lives in the way of Allah, and they said: 'Do not march forth in the heat.' Say: 'The fire of Hell is more intense in heat.' If only they had understood.

key_terms.الْمُخَلَّفُونَ: Those who were left behind (non-combatants who stayed home)
key_terms.لَا تَنْفِرُوا: Do not march forth / Do not set out
key_terms.يُجَاهِدُوا: To strive/jihad (in the way of God)

ai.seo_question: What is the meaning of 'Do not march forth in the heat' in Surat al-Tawbah?
ai.summary: In the context of the Expedition of Tabuk, this verse critiques the hypocrites (Munafiqun) who rejoiced in their absence from the Prophet, prioritizing worldly comfort over spiritual duty. The Quranic response, 'Fire of Hell is more intense,' serves as a logical deduction (qiyas) urging them to reflect on the eternal consequences of their negligence. This highlights the Shia emphasis on the transition from mere physical presence to sincere internal conviction in the path of Allah.
